question: A man goes to Chennai from Hyderabad at a speed of 24km/hr and returns to Hyderabad at speed of 40km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same in both directions, the average speed is given directly by the formula:

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 24 × 40) ÷ (24 + 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 1920 ÷ 64 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Hyderabad to Chennai (S₁) = 24 km/hr

Speed from Chennai to Hyderabad (S₂) = 40 km/hr

Let the one-way distance between the two cities be D km.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for the forward journey (T₁) = D ÷ 24

⇒ Time taken for the return journey (T₂) = D ÷ 40

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 24) + (D ÷ 40)

⇒ Total Time = (5D + 3D) ÷ 120

⇒ Total Time = 8D ÷ 120 = D ÷ 15

⇒ Total Distance covered = D + D = 2D

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (D ÷ 15)

⇒ Average Speed = 2 × 15 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If an object covers three equal parts of a journey at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is calculated as (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed with Different Distances

If an object travels variable distances d₁, d₂, d₃ taking corresponding times t₁, t₂, t₃, the Average Speed is strictly given by (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃).

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (x + y). When moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (x − y).
